clue.text: Account given by cold, mistreated pet bear

parts.note: standard abbreviation for account

indicators.note: something mistreated has been knocked about, so the word beside it is scrambled

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of a pet bear left out in the cold and badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal in the story, but it is the verb meaning to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or put up with it, which is a sense of the verb accept.

clue.text: One hearing riot breaking out after Audrey's cut in half

indicators.note: cutting a name in half leaves only its front half standing

parts.note: the name, of which only the first three of six letters are kept

indicators.note: a riot breaking out is disorder, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone listening as trouble erupts after Audrey has had a drastic haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Audrey is cut in half to AUD, and the jumbled riot follows it, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is literally a listener, from Latin audire, to hear, as at a hearing or an audited course.

clue.text: Turn up in pursuit of shy animal

parts.note: coy means bashful or shy

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An instruction to appear while chasing some timid creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In pursuit of' means following, so the turned-round up comes after the word for shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent, also called nutria, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Suffragette traps hunk dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and end up in a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A campaigning woman catches a handsome man on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' looks like the verb whose subject is the suffragette, but it is only fodder for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmeline Pankhurst led the British campaign for votes for women in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Mother has fifty small offspring that suckle

definitions.note: loose: mammals are the creatures whose offspring suckle

parts.note: an affectionate word for mother
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A mother with a great many little children, all at the breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammals are the class of animals whose young feed on milk from the mother's body.

clue.text: Sailor's companion's fate

parts.note: a mate is a friend or companion
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Wondering what became of a seaman's shipmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 's is the definition's link ('Sailor is'); the second joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, borrowed from French, for a sailor in the navy.

clue.text: Virgin maintaining resistance to wed

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A chaste woman still resisting getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' could be any virgin; here it is the Virgin, Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to marry, a straightforward synonym for joining in matrimony.

clue.text: Radon made newly formed galaxy

indicators.note: something newly formed has been made over, so these letters are put together afresh

parts.note: nine letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A radioactive gas has produced a brand-new galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest large spiral galaxy to our own Milky Way.

clue.text: Supplies with plants

definitions.meaning: first meaning: provides or keeps goods for sale
second meaning: scented garden flowers of the cabbage family

explanation.surface: Someone provisions a garden with plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it is gardening; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop stocks goods, supplying them, and stocks are also fragrant flowering garden plants.

clue.text: Obtained meat in Batman's New York?

parts.note: got is the past tense of get, to obtain
ham is cured pork, a meat

explanation.surface: Buying some meat in the fictional home of Batman.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotham City, Batman's home, is modelled on New York, which has long carried the nickname Gotham.

clue.text: Abstaining from booze with Dr Young? It's incredible

indicators.note: something incredible is beyond belief, so the letters are taken to be wildly reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a certain Dr Young has given up drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the fodder to its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drying out is the idiom for going through a period of abstinence to recover from heavy drinking.

clue.text: Heads of research and development inveighing against old means of spreading the word

indicators.note: heads are the tops of things, so only the leading letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the leading letter of each of these four words
the leading letter of this word

explanation.surface: Senior figures in an R&D department railing against outdated ways of communicating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the final letter; 'against' is skipped as a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio broadcasting is a medium for spreading news and messages to many listeners at once.

clue.text: Time woman accepted reality?

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman finally comes to terms with how things really are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepted' looks like the woman's verb, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Truth is what is accepted as fact or actuality, so it can be called the accepted reality.

clue.text: Plant wine plant

parts.note: holly is an evergreen plant
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Instructions to bury a bottle of wine in the garden, then a second instruction to plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised first Plant is wordplay and the final plant is the definition, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall garden flower of the mallow family, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Stage for Roy Orbison's openers to play guitar

indicators.note: openers come first, so only the starting letter of each name is kept

parts.note: the starting letters of the singer's two names
to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: A platform set up for Roy Orbison's supporting acts to play guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openers' suggests opening acts at a concert; here it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or performer, a kind of stage.

clue.text: Gorgeous bird seen at championship game in America

parts.note: superb means magnificent or gorgeous
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A beautiful bird spotted at a big American sporting final.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the annual championship game of American football's NFL.

clue.text: So-called diplomacy changed course

indicators.note: so-called means named or said, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, and said aloud it matches the sailing verb

explanation.surface: A supposedly diplomatic approach that switched direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat tacks by turning into the wind to change its heading, so tacked means changed course.

clue.text: Pale actor playing old queen

indicators.note: playing suggests acting out a part, so the letters take on a different arrangement

parts.note: nine letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pallid performer cast as an ancient monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of ancient Egypt, dying in 30 BC.

clue.text: Put in amount of phlegm

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a sum is an amount
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's note to add some quantity of mucus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is the medical term for phlegm or mucus coughed up from the lungs.

clue.text: Rug is used by Home Counties painter

parts.note: a mat is a small rug
taken as written
the Home Counties around London are in the South East of England

explanation.surface: A rug in the home of a painter living near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, so SE stands for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a leading French painter of the twentieth century, known for bold colour.

clue.text: Look closely at date of Debrett's book?

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
a date or period of time, an age

explanation.surface: Checking the publication date of a well-known reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: Debrett's is a British publisher whose best-known title, Debrett's Peerage, lists the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags that Peerage is one example of a Debrett's publication, its famous guide to titled families.

clue.text: Where sailors are extremely likely to find stout

parts.note: sailors are found in port when ashore

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, so only its two end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Where sailors would most probably go for a pint of dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer, the drink a sailor in port might seek; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly and stout both describe a person who is rather fat or heavily built.

clue.text: Serious attention given to home for brood

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give them attention
a nest is the home where a bird raises its brood

explanation.surface: Solemn care devoted to providing a home for one's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intention or manner.

clue.text: Fights for discarded bits of food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal word for brawls or scuffles
second meaning: leftovers thrown away after a meal

explanation.surface: Animals brawling over leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fight over food; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are informal fights, and scraps are also the leftover morsels of a meal.

clue.text: After fish, go into chippy

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to go into

explanation.surface: Having bought fish, someone heads into the fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a chippy is a fish-and-chip shop, which the fish suggests; it is also slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British informal slang for a woodworker, from the chips of wood the trade produces.

clue.text: Irene manages to hold injected fluid

indicators.note: the words are said to hold the solution, which lies inside them across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the name and the start of the verb

explanation.surface: Irene succeeds in keeping a liquid inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is liquid introduced into the rectum, so it is a fluid that is injected.

clue.text: Previous rip-off associated with gold

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of place, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An earlier swindle involving gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip-off' reads as one word meaning a con, but it splits into rip and the signal off.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier in time or order, a direct synonym of previous.

clue.text: Flower given to husband from Dublin, perhaps

parts.note: the iris is a flower
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife from Dublin receives flowers from her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital of Ireland, so someone from there is an example of an Irish person.

clue.text: First of amorous lovers only now experiencing being single

indicators.note: first of means the leading letter is taken from each of the following words

parts.note: the leading letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Lovers who have only now discovered what it is to be single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' looks as if it applies only to amorous, but it takes the opening letter of all five words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be single is to be on one's own, unaccompanied, which is what alone means.

clue.text: I also tire when playing patience

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: nine letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits getting bored with a card game too.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is the British name for the one-player card game Americans call solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire and patience are two names for the same single-player card game.

clue.text: Wild fellow claiming a number of discarded things for collection

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so one part is held inside the other

parts.note: a savage is a wild, untamed person
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a number

explanation.surface: A rough character grabbing a pile of rubbish to collect.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is material rescued from waste or wreckage and gathered for reuse.

clue.text: A revolutionary appearing in court gains prestige

indicators.note: appearing in places one part within the other

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
taken as written
Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel on trial wins himself renown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means distinction or prestige, the quality of being admired.
